overview: ASX Limited is the operator of Australia's primary securities exchange and the country's central market infrastructure provider, running listings, cash equities and derivatives trading, central counterparty clearing, settlement/registry, and market data & technology services under an integrated, vertically-linked model. It holds market licences, clearing and settlement facility licences and a benchmark administrator licence, placing it under direct oversight of ASIC and the RBA. ASX itself is a listed company trading on the exchange it operates, generating FY26 operating revenue of A$1.25 billion across four segments: Listings, Markets, Technology & Data, and Securities & Payments.

business_model.summary: ASX earns largely recurring, fee-based revenue from being the mandatory or default gateway for Australian capital formation, trading and post-trade infrastructure: listing fees (initial, annual, secondary raisings), trading and clearing fees on cash equities and derivatives, settlement/registry/Austraclear fees, and data/connectivity fees. Much of the base (annual listing fees, technology hosting/connectivity, data subscriptions, CHESS registry) is highly recurring and non-discretionary for participants, while trading-linked and capital-raising revenue (futures volumes, IPOs, secondary raisings) is more transactional and cyclical with market activity and volatility. Net interest income on cash balances and participant collateral is a smaller, separately disclosed, rate-sensitive income stream (FY26: A$73.2m, down 15.7% YoY).

revenue_streams.name: Securities & Payments (CCP clearing, settlement, Austraclear, issuer services)

business_model.customer_type: B2B — listed issuers/companies, trading participants (banks, brokers, market makers), clearing/settlement participants, data vendors and institutional investors; effectively the whole Australian financial services industry is a customer or counterparty
business_model.geographic_mix: Almost entirely Australia-domestic (ASX operates Australian and some New Zealand market infrastructure); revenue is AUD-denominated with limited direct FX exposure, though international listings and global data distribution provide some offshore revenue

main_competitors: Cboe Australia / TMX Australia Exchange (formerly Chi-X)
Global exchange groups for dual/secondary listings (LSE, NASDAQ, HKEX)
competitive_position.market_position: Near-monopoly in Australian primary listings, and sole provider of cash equities clearing (CCP) and settlement/sub-register services (CHESS) in Australia; dominant but no longer sole venue for cash equities trading, where Cboe Australia (now TMX Australia Exchange after TMX Group's August 2026 acquisition) holds roughly 20% of on-market cash equities turnover.

moat_factors.factor: Regulatory licence / natural monopoly in clearing & settlement
moat_factors.description: ASX is the sole holder of cash equities CCP clearing and CHESS settlement/registry licences in Australia; new entry requires clearing new market and prudential regulatory licences, an extremely high bar, and CHESS underpins legal title for >20 million unique security holdings

Deep liquidity pool, broad institutional/retail investor base and large existing issuer cohort make ASX the default primary listing venue for Australian companies, reinforcing itself as capital and secondary trading concentrate there

Trading participants, registries, data vendors and superannuation funds have systems and processes built around ASX's CHESS, Austraclear and connectivity infrastructure (Australian Liquidity Centre), making migration costly and slow
Long-standing status as steward of critical market infrastructure, though materially dented by the ASIC Inquiry findings, misleading-conduct penalty and heightened scrutiny through FY26
Australian Liquidity Centre co-location, ASX Net global distribution and integrated data products create a scale advantage difficult for niche competitors to replicate

weaknesses: Elevated and rising cost base (total expenses up 21.1% in FY26) driven by technology modernisation, the Accelerate Program and regulatory remediation, compressing margins (EBIT margin down 280bps to 55.6%)

History of major technology project failure (original CHESS replacement abandoned in 2022) has damaged credibility and invited direct regulatory rule-making (ASIC's 2025 clearing & settlement access/pricing rules) that erodes pricing power
Regulatory-mandated additional A$150 million capital buffer through FY27 constrains capital return (dividend payout ratio range cut from 80-90% to 75-85%)
Loss of trading market share to Cboe Australia (~20% of cash equities turnover) in the one segment where ASX faces direct competition
Leadership discontinuity — CEO departure, interim CEO period and external hire (Anthony Attia, ex-Euronext) commencing September 2026 creates execution and cultural-transition risk

growth_drivers: Structural tailwind from Australia's compulsory superannuation pool (A$4.4 trillion, forecast to reach ~A$12 trillion over 20 years), supporting long-term capital markets activity and listings
Recovery in IPO and listings activity — FY26 saw 100 new listed entities (+44.9% YoY), the strongest year since FY22, with A$5.6 billion of IPO capital raised, above the five-year average
Derivatives (futures and OTC) volume growth amid interest-rate volatility — Markets revenue up 18.6% in FY26, the fastest-growing segment
Technology & Data expansion — new microwave connectivity, debt-market activity data products, growing ALC co-location demand, and record 72 new ETF listings

Post-CHESS-Release-1 platform reuse — cloud, data, integration and observability capabilities built for CHESS now support other technology modernisation (e.g., TradeAccept replacement, ASX Trade cash-market platform upgrade)
New product areas: electricity futures contracts, ASX-Bloomberg AusBond Index Futures, SOFIA overnight repo benchmark, and early moves into collateral tokenisation via Austraclear

Potential easing of the A$150 million capital charge and payout-ratio constraint as Accelerate Program milestones are met and ASIC/RBA approve staged release, which would support dividend growth from FY28

business.description: CHESS Release 2 (settlement/sub-register) remains outstanding after Release 1 (clearing) went live April 2026; Drop 5 documentation has already slipped to October 2026, and the original CHESS project failure (abandoned 2022) shows the scale of execution risk in such programs

Cboe Australia (now TMX Australia Exchange, ~20% market share) continues to compete for order flow in ASX-listed securities, pressuring trading fee economics even though clearing/settlement remains ASX's monopoly
Technology, Accelerate Program, and regulatory remediation costs pushed FY26 total expenses up 21.1%; management flags the cost profile as an 'ongoing focus,' with no clear near-term reversal

financial.description: ASIC-mandated accumulation of an extra A$150 million in net tangible assets by 30 June 2027 forced a cut in the dividend payout ratio policy (80-90% to 75-85%), directly reducing near-term shareholder distributions
Net interest income fell 15.7% in FY26 on lower average RBA cash rates and higher lease finance costs; further rate cuts would continue to pressure this income line

Cash and financial assets fell 23.4% YoY on lower participant margin balances; a shift back to directional exposure or market stress could swing collateral-related interest income and balance sheet size

regulatory.risk: Ongoing regulatory scrutiny and remediation obligations
regulatory.description: The nine-month ASIC Inquiry (concluded April 2026) mandated a comprehensive remediation package — governance uplift of clearing/settlement boards, leadership capability, Accelerate Program reset, and the A$150m capital charge — with milestones subject to ongoing ASIC/RBA assessment

ASX admitted misleading conduct over 2022 CHESS project statements and paid a $20.5 million penalty plus $3 million in ASIC costs (settled June/July 2026); reputational and precedent risk for future market disclosures remains

ASIC's 2025 clearing & settlement rules require ASX to provide transparent, fair, non-discriminatory pricing and access, and technology designed to facilitate third-party access — potentially limiting ASX's ability to monetise its infrastructure monopoly as freely as before

regulatory.risk: Listing rule and governance reform overhang
regulatory.description: Proposed listing rule changes (dilutive takeover thresholds, foreign exempt listing approvals) and ASX's new role overseeing the fifth edition of the Corporate Governance Principles add complexity and stakeholder-management burden

macro.description: Listings and secondary capital-raising revenue depend on IPO windows and market sentiment; a downturn in risk appetite would reduce new listing and capital-raising fee income
Falling RBA cash rates compress net interest income on ASX's own cash and participant collateral balances, a direct drag on statutory/underlying profit
While elevated volatility generally boosts derivatives and cash equities trading volumes (a FY26 tailwind), extreme dislocation could also raise margin/collateral and operational risk

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Australian capital markets infrastructure is a structurally growing but heavily regulated industry, underpinned by the world's 5th-largest (forecast 2nd-largest by early 2030s) compulsory superannuation pool; global market-infrastructure peers face similar themes of tokenisation, real-time settlement, and regulatory-driven competition in post-trade services
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate — recurring listing/data/technology fees provide a defensive base (~50-60% of revenue), while trading volumes, IPO activity and secondary capital raisings are cyclical and sentiment-driven
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate direct exposure via net interest income on own cash and participant collateral balances (FY26: A$73.2m, ~6% of underlying pre-tax profit, but volatile); indirect sensitivity via capital markets activity levels
key_input_costs: Occupancy (new Sydney head office at 39 Martin Place)

recent_developments.event: Anthony Attia (former Euronext leader) commenced as Managing Director and CEO on 1 September 2026, succeeding interim CEO Darren Yip after Helen Lofthouse's May 2026 departure

FY26 full-year results: operating revenue $1,254.6m (+13.3%), underlying NPAT $536.4m (+5.2%), statutory NPAT $484.9m (-3.5%) after $51.5m of significant items; dividend payout ratio range cut to 75-85% of underlying NPAT to fund the ASIC capital charge
TMX Group completed acquisition of Cboe Australia (renamed TMX Australia Exchange), ASX's primary cash-equities trading competitor with ~20% market share
Federal Court approved settlement of ASIC proceedings over misleading 2022 CHESS project disclosures; ASX paid $20.5m penalty plus $3.0m towards ASIC's legal costs
ASX admitted misleading conduct relating to the original (abandoned) CHESS replacement project, contravening ASIC Act sections 12DA/12DB

ASIC's nine-month Inquiry into ASX's governance, capability and risk management concluded; ASX committed to a remediation package including an additional A$150m capital buffer, independent Clearing & Settlement Boards and a reset Accelerate Program

CHESS Release 1 (clearing services) went live 20 April 2026, with all Approved Market Operators successfully connected — the first major delivered milestone of the long-delayed CHESS replacement program; Release 2 (settlement/sub-register) targeted later with Drop 5 documentation slipping to October 2026
Sale of ASX's 49.4% interest in Sympli (electronic property conveyancing JV) agreed, completed July 2026, contributing to a $13.3m significant-item loss

Board renewal: new non-executive directors Anne Loveridge, Dee McGrath and former Cboe Australia CEO Vic Jokovic appointed; independent Clearing & Settlement Facility Boards established (no ASX directors) with new appointees John Cincotta and Lisa Wade

items.period: FY2027 and beyond (next two dividends expected at bottom of range)
items.notes: Cut from the prior 80-90% policy range in December 2025 to help fund the ASIC-mandated A$150m additional capital accumulation by 30 June 2027; management flagged payout ratio to remain at the bottom of the new range for at least the next two dividends

items.target: A$150 million of additional net tangible assets vs 31 Dec 2025 base
items.notes: Capital charge imposed as part of ASIC Inquiry remediation; will be held until Accelerate Program milestones are achieved and ASIC approves staged reduction or release

items.target: Reset program agreed with ASIC and RBA, effective 1 July 2026
items.notes: Clearer definition of success and measurable outcomes; achievement of milestones directly linked to reducing/removing the $150m capital charge

items.target: No specific numeric target disclosed; management states elevated cost profile 'remains an ongoing focus'
items.notes: FY26 total expenses rose 21.1%, including one-off ASIC Inquiry costs of $30.8m; some of this (Inquiry-specific costs) should not recur in FY27, but Accelerate Program and technology modernisation spend is expected to continue

guidance.management_commentary: Chair David Clarke: ASX enters FY27 with 'positive momentum' following CHESS Release 1 delivery, the new CEO appointment, resolution of ASIC litigation and the Accelerate Program reset, but flagged FY26 total shareholder returns were below expectations and reiterated commitment to disciplined execution and rebuilding accountability. Interim CEO Darren Yip highlighted 'strong sense of optimism' about the outlook given the recovery in listings and capital markets activity, while noting the elevated cost profile remains a senior management focus. No explicit quantitative FY27 revenue, NPAT or margin guidance was provided in the results materials reviewed.

bull_case: Quasi-monopoly economics in Australian listings, clearing and settlement provide durable, largely non-discretionary recurring revenue with high structural barriers to entry

FY26 showed broad-based growth across all four segments (revenue +13.3%) with listings activity at its strongest since FY22 and derivatives volumes benefiting from rate volatility — a sign underlying franchise demand remains intact despite governance turmoil

New external CEO (Anthony Attia, deep exchange/post-trade experience from Euronext/ICE/NYSE) plus a reconstituted, more independent Board and Clearing & Settlement Boards could accelerate execution discipline and eventually unwind the $150m capital charge, restoring higher payout ratios
Long-run structural tailwind from Australia's growing compulsory superannuation pool (forecast toward A$12 trillion) supports secular growth in capital formation, trading and data demand
CHESS Release 1 (clearing) is now live, removing one major source of multi-year technology overhang and unlocking reusable cloud/data platform investment for further modernisation
bear_case: CHESS Release 2 (settlement/sub-register, the more complex component) is still pending, with milestone slippage (Drop 5 documentation moved to October 2026) showing execution risk on critical infrastructure has not been fully resolved

Elevated and rising cost base (total expenses +21.1% in FY26) is compressing margins and shows no clear near-term reversal, even as ASIC Inquiry-specific costs roll off, given ongoing Accelerate Program and technology modernisation spend

Regulatory capital charge and reduced payout ratio (75-85% vs prior 80-90%) directly constrain near-term shareholder returns, with the timeline and conditions for release dependent on ASIC/RBA approval, an external and uncertain gate

Cboe Australia's (now TMX Australia Exchange) ~20% share of cash equities trading shows ASX's monopoly is not absolute even in its core market, and ASIC's 2025 access/pricing rules limit ASX's ability to leverage infrastructure dominance commercially

Reputational damage from the ASIC Inquiry findings, admitted misleading conduct and CEO transition creates ongoing governance and execution uncertainty just as a new, externally-hired CEO begins a difficult turnaround
